items.title: leviathan
items.description: **Deep memory for agents over large datasets.**   Leviathan is a single static binary that turns your records (JSONL, JSON, CSV/TSV, SQLite, or anything a database CLI can export) into a ranked full-text index.
items.summary: Leviathan is a single static binary that converts various data formats into a ranked full-text index, enabling agents to handle large datasets efficiently. The sources highlight that AI agent memory is a persistent storage layer that retains information across sessions, allowing agents to remember user interactions and preferences. This memory is separate from the model’s context window and includes procedural memory for consistent application of workflows and processes. The sources also mention that Leviathan excels at turning records into a ranked full-text index, which is crucial for agents to retrieve information over time independent of the LLM’s limited context window.

It uses a coding agent to prepare the avatar from your image and a local editor with live preview for fine-tuning. The process involves four steps: the coding agent creates the avatar from the image, and the local editor allows for fine-tuning. items.title: SCM
items.description: Deep AI search for every photo and every frame of video in any folder on macOS
items.summary: SCM, an MIT-licensed Electron app for macOS, indexes every photo and every video frame in watched folders on-device to enable offline CLIP search. It retrieves matching stills and video moments without cloud calls, offering five search modes: Files, Scenes, OCR via Tesseract in 35+ languages, Dialogue via Whisper transcription, and an optional local LLMs 'Ask' chat. The default model is CLIP ViT-L/14@336, with 480-570ms per image on CPU, and SigLIP variants for speed/detail trade-offs. SCM targets folders, external-drive archives, and other collections outside Apple Photos, providing local retrieval systems across user-selected folders.

items.title: pi-pocket
items.description: A durable, multiplayer, mobile-first web app for Pi agents, built on Pi Durable
items.summary: Pi Durable is an experimental framework from Arendelle, released alongside Pi 1.0, for building applications around agent conversations that need to survive restarts. It treats conversations as durable state, allowing them to be checkpointed, resumed after a crash, and run multiple at once, each with its own model, tools, instructions, and working directory. It is a standalone framework meant for applications that need agent conversations to persist across process restarts, support multiple simultaneous conversations, or let more than one client observe and steer the same session. It is an experimental, MIT-licensed foundation for long-running agent apps with checkpoints and resumable tasks.

items.title: Chat_UI
items.description: The fastest and litest LLM chating ui with 2 fields, less than 100 kb and completely no dependent.
items.summary: The sources mention several open-source LLM chat UIs, but none specifically match the criteria of being the fastest, lightest, with only two fields, less than 100 KB, and completely no dependent. Open WebUI is noted for its speed and large community, while huggingface/chat-ui is a TypeScript/SvelteKit application with 10.8k GitHub stars and 1.7k forks. Vercel Chatbot and assistant-ui are also mentioned for their features, but none explicitly meet the described lightweight and dependency-free requirements.

items.title: Gemini-Config-Checker
items.description: Chain region scanner: find proxy configs that get you into Google AI Studio and Gemini (signed-in browser check, anti-DPI, Windows/macOS/Linux/Android)
items.summary: The GitHub repository for Gemini-Config-Checker provides details on a chain region scanner that finds proxy configurations to access Google AI Studio and Gemini, including signed-in browser checks and anti-DPI measures for Windows, macOS, Linux, and Android. It mentions optional repository secrets for Android signatures. The Google support thread suggests verifying region and age settings, using different browsers, and clearing cache/cookies to access Google AI Studio. The Google AI Developers Forum mentions issues with region/age restrictions and potential organizational policy flags for regional access review.

items.title: box
items.description: Run AI agents in a sandbox that restricts what they can execute, read, write, and reach on the network. Box combines OS isolation with default-deny Dogwood policies and credential injection that keeps secrets outside the agent. Written in Rust. Supports macOS on Apple silicon, with Linux support planned.
items.summary: Strands Box is an open source sandbox for AI agents that combines operating-system isolation with fine-grained policies for governing agent actions. It uses OS-level isolation, such as macOS Seatbelt, to define what the agent can reach, on the host machine and on the network. It is written in Rust and currently supports macOS on Apple silicon, with Linux support planned. Box embeds the Dogwood Local Engine to enforce allow or deny decisions around the running agent. The setup is available for installation on Mac, Linux, or WSL with pre-configured coding and agent workflows.

items.title: 4DCodeBench
items.description: 4DCodeBench: Benchmarking Agents on Inverse Graphics of Dynamic Scenes
items.summary: 4DCodeBench is a benchmark for 4D inverse graphics through code generation, where agents reconstruct dynamic scenes from video as executable graphics programs. The benchmark comprises 200 dynamic scenes—100 real videos and 100 synthetic scenes with 4D ground truth—spanning diverse materials, interactions, and physical phenomena. Agents must translate visual observations into compact representations of scene structure and dynamics, implementing abstractions such as physical simulations to reproduce complex behavior. The benchmark evaluates whether agents can interpret the dynamics of the world through code, testing if they can write executable graphics code that specifies the scene's geometry, how that geometry changes over time, and how to render it, without access to the reference video.

items.title: ai-iso-skill
items.description: Claude skill that draws interactive isometric figures in a single HTML file
items.summary: The sources indicate that the drawio-skill is an agent skill that can generate interactive isometric figures in a single HTML file. It is designed to turn various sources into editable, tested draw.io architecture diagrams, including natural language, code, Terraform/K8s, SQL, OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, Protobuf, and GraphQL. The skill supports multiple platforms and includes features like incremental sync, multi-view projection, drift diff, CI architecture tests, and interactive HTML exports. It is complemented by the official jgraph plugin for additional functionality. The skill is implemented in a single SKILL.md file with no need for an MCP server.

items.title: Sentry
items.description: Learning to Recover from LLM Agent Failures at Test Time
items.summary: The paper "Sentry: Learning to Recover from LLM Agent Failures at Test Time" by Changxiu Ji et al. introduces Sentry, a failure-management layer that detects failures in LLM agents and retrieves lessons from an external playbook to guide recovery. Sentry verifies if the agent has recovered without task rewards and stores new lessons only if successful. The paper does not provide specific figures or metrics on the performance improvements of Sentry over baselines. Another source mentions a framework called AgentDebug that provides corrective feedback and shows improvements in task success, but does not directly compare it to Sentry. The sources do not provide a definitive answer on how Sentry specifically compares to other methods in terms of performance improvements.

items.title: openpactprotocol
items.description: PACT is an open protocol for personal agents to interact with businesses’ agents under explicit, verifiable user permissions.
items.summary: PACT is an open protocol for personal agents to interact with businesses’ agents under explicit, verifiable user permissions. It is built on the Agent2Agent protocol and OAuth 2.0, allowing businesses to verify whom a personal agent represents and what that customer has authorized it to do. It is an open standard defining how personal AI agents authenticate with businesses and what actions those businesses permit the agents to take. The protocol is supported by companies like Genesys, Instinct, Rocket, Shopify, Stripe, and Walmart. The sources do not provide specific dates for the rollout or version numbers beyond mentioning a v0.1 specification due this month.
